correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=2, a forbidden gcd is at least its least obstruction. Counting nonempty subsets of multiples of that obstruction and using a union bound gives exact two-sided powers-of-two estimates, with the extra unit accounting for the empty subset. Taking logarithms yields the uniform O(log n/n) exponent comparison. The r=k fiber is exactly divisible by L_(k-1) but not L_k; lcm increases exactly at prime powers. The least-prime fibers have the stated finite inclusion-exclusion densities. Both missing tails tend to zero, proving weak convergence. Even/odd bounds follow globally. The standalone stdlib checker independently enumerated subset gcds for n<=16, used Möbius counts and bounds for n<=1500, and confirmed exact finite arithmetic fibers for n<=200000; it is not substituted for proof.

value.rationale: The exact atom-and-weight distribution determines a natural invariant of a ratio explicitly singled out in a published open question, with no input-size restriction. It completely identifies the negative prime-power and positive odd-prime regimes and supplies quantitative exponential bounds proving both extreme limits. This exceeds finite tabulation, a textbook normalization check, and sign-only comparisons; no unsolved summatory claim is asserted.
